about: Values the Python and JavaScript bindings must agree on. This file is the only place they are written; tools/generate.py writes python/bollardeck/constants.py and js/bollardeck.constants.js from it, and the constants block inside js/bollardeck.js.

HOLD_MS.about: A press this long or longer is a hold, not a tap.

TAP_FOLLOW_MS.about: Taps on one button chain when the next press begins within this long of the last release.

PRESS_MATCH_MS.about: A release that states its own time belongs to an announced press when the press it describes began within this long of the announcement.

PRESS_LOST_MS.about: A press a key source announced is forgotten when its release has not come after this long.

TAP_CHAIN_MAX.about: The longest chain of taps that is one gesture: a triple. A fourth tap starts a new chain.

CUE_STATES.about: The states a button cue can be in.

CUE_ROLES.about: What a lit button can stand for. A cue may also carry no role (null).

PULSE_PERIOD_MS.about: One breath of a pulse cue: 2 Hz.

CHASE_PERIOD_MS.about: One turn of a chase cue.

PULSE_FLOOR.about: How bright a pulse cue is at its dimmest, where full is 1.

CHASE_TAIL.about: How bright the lamps behind a chase cue's head are, where the head is 1.

CHASE_STEPS.about: The lamps in a button's arc: a chase cue's head visits each once per turn.

BUTTON_NUMBERS.about: The three buttons. A button is its number everywhere on the SDK's surface: cues, key events, gesture names.

BUTTONS.about: One row per button. "button" is the one vocabulary (1, 2, 3). "label" is a name for people and describes the Boll's medallion only. "wire" is the word the bollardeck/1 wire uses for the button under "btn" (spec/bollardeck.md, 6.2), and "id" is its wire id; both are for translating at the wire, stay for as long as the wire is bollardeck/1, and are not a second vocabulary.

GESTURES.about: Every gesture name: tap<button> for one tap, tap<button>x<count> for a chain of 2 or 3 taps, hold<button> for a hold.

PROMPT_KINDS.about: The kinds of prompt the keymap gives meanings for.

KEYMAP.about: The engagement keymap, version 2: what each gesture means. "prompt" applies while a prompt is showing and gives one meaning per kind of prompt: {"choice": x} answers the prompt with x, {"do": name} is a verb ("raw": this kind wants press and release times, not gestures), null takes the gesture and does nothing. "idle" (no prompt showing) and "always" (both, and first) map a gesture to a verb. "pocket" (optional) maps a gesture to a player verb when no prompt is showing and the device is in the pocket context (a cart with no dock), and is looked at before "idle". It fits schema/keymap.schema.json.

KEYMAP_CONTEXTS.about: The device contexts a keymap may give meanings for besides idle; a resolver is told the context, and with none given only prompt, idle and always apply.

AUDIO_ROUTES.about: Where a cart's sound can go: the dock's audio, the headphone jack, a Bluetooth headset or speaker, USB-C headphones on the side port, or nowhere. One route plays at a time.

POWER_SOURCES.about: Where a device's power comes from now: a mains adapter, a dock's Bollport, a USB-C charger or computer on a side port, its own battery pack, or a board that cannot tell.

CART_ROLES.about: The role a cart picks from what is on its Bollport (spec v0.3 §5.3): host and brain of a dock, a guest under another cart, a screen or hub with no dock descriptor, nothing at all (pocket), or off. A computer on either port is an overlay, not a role.

POCKET_VERBS.about: The player verbs of the pocket context: what a player (Pompa on a cart) does for each. whats_on shows the title, the audio route and the battery; share queues a share until the device is online; pair starts pairing the cart with a person's Pop Boll account (HAMS pairing).

HELP_DETECTORS.about: The struggle detectors bollardeck.help ships (help-pack/1 scenarios name one of these, or a detector a page registers with a name starting x-). Each is a pure function of the event stream and the clock.

HELP_PILLS_AT_ONCE.about: How many help offers (the small HELP? button by a control) a page shows at once.

HELP_OFFERS_PER_VIEW.about: The most help offers one page view makes, however many struggles are detected (an offer withdrawn because a quiet zone began does not count).

HELP_BACKOFF_IGNORES.about: Offers in a row, of any topic, left to fade that make the whole engine back off.

HELP_BACKOFF_MS.about: The first back-off: no offers at all for this long (a day). Each back-off after it doubles, until an offer is opened.

HELP_EVENTS_MAX.about: The most events an engine keeps, whatever its window: a page left open for hours stays as cheap as a new one.

HELP_TOPIC_COOLDOWN_MS.about: After a topic is offered, it is not offered again for this long (one day).

HELP_SNOOZE_MS.about: NOT NOW on a help box, or HELP_IGNORES_TO_SNOOZE ignored offers, keep its topic quiet this long (seven days).

HELP_IGNORES_TO_SNOOZE.about: Offers of one topic left to fade on their own that snooze the topic.

HELP_OFFER_MS.about: How long an offer stays up before it fades by itself (counted as ignored).

HELP_LANDING_QUIET_MS.about: No offers this soon after a page loads, except from the idle-after-landing detector.

HELP_READ_MS.about: A help box open this long (or its tour or video watched halfway) counts as read: its topic is not offered again unless the struggle comes back.

HELP_RECUR_DAYS.about: A read topic is offered again once its struggle has been detected on this many different later days (UTC days), or when its rev rises.

HELP_SAY_MS_PER_WORD.about: A director script's say step stays up this long per word, unless the step gives its own ms.

HELP_SAY_MIN_MS.about: The shortest a say step stays up.

HELP_SAY_MAX_CHARS.about: The longest text one say step may carry.

HELP_CAPTION_LINE.about: The longest caption line, in characters; a caption cue is at most two lines.

HELP_SCRIPT_MAX_MS.about: The longest a director script may run in recorded time (every say, wait and hold, not cut).

HELP_DIRECTOR_VERBS.about: The steps a help-director/1 script may take.

HELP_HOLD_MS.about: Each director verb's default hold after it is done, in ms (a say step's hold is its reading time instead).
